title: No Clock-Ins, No Micromanaging, & 100-Year Sweaters: Inside Brunello Cucinelli’s Anti-Corporate Fashion House
text:
No Clock-Ins, No Micromanaging, & 100-Year Sweaters: Inside Brunello Cucinelli’s Anti-Corporate Fashion House

Let’s be honest: when most of us hear “Italian luxury knitwear titan,” our brains don’t immediately leap to labor rights, workplace dignity, or radical empathy. We think of four-figure price tags and pristine neutral palettes that live strictly in the closets of the top 1%.

So while watching the new documentary on Brunello Cucinelli (Brunello: The Gracious Visionary), I wasn’t necessarily expecting a masterclass on how to treat human beings with basic dignity. But that is precisely what makes Cucinelli’s story so fascinating, and why it feels like such an antidote to the fast pace of the fashion industry.

At the core of this film is a concept Cucinelli calls “Humanistic Capitalism.” It sounds like a lofty corporate buzzword until you actually look at how his house operates. In an industry where burnout is often treated like a badge of honor and modern hustle culture demands we grind ourselves into dust, Cucinelli has spent decades proving a radically simple point: You can build a billion-dollar empire without exploiting the people who build it for you.

Before he was the “King of Cashmere,” Cucinelli was just a scrappy young guy trying to break into the market. Founded in the late 1970s and scaling through the ’80s, the brand’s origins carry an ambitious charm. In the early days, he would literally change his voice on phone calls, pretending to be different secretaries and executives to create the illusion that he was running a massive, established enterprise.

As a great philosopher once said, “Delulu is the solulu,” because it worked. During his first showcase, he managed to sell over 11,000 sweaters—in just two days. Manufacturing early demand through sheer audacity paid off and led to him making a legendary American debut at Barneys New York (RIP to the iconic fashion mecca).

Staying true to his values, Cucinelli would tell investors “If you’re after a business that profits at the expense of humanity, this is not the company you should invest in.”

When he launched his brand in 1978, fashion moved at a completely different pace. Fast-fashion, micro-trends, weekly drops, and viral $10 internet hauls weren’t even on the horizon. Garments were bought with care, repaired when worn, and expected to hold their ground over time. But still, Cucinelli wanted to push that ethos to the extreme, asking his mother to help him create a sweater designed to last 100 years.

In an era saturated with cheap, disposable clothing that pills after two washes, the concept of a 100-year garment isn’t just about high-end craftsmanship. It’s an act of anti-capitalist resistance against consumerism. It asks us to re-evaluate our entire relationship with what we buy.

As a Shopping Director, a huge part of my daily life is centered on vetting trends, testing products, and telling you what’s actually worth putting in your cart. But lately, my personal editorial ethos has shifted from simply asking, “What else do we need to buy?” to “How can we buy better, not more?”

It’s an idea that actress Liu Tao echoes in the documentary when reflecting on why Brunello Cucinelli resonates so deeply: “This brand flatters my body’s proportions and gives me confidence. That’s why I love this brand.” True luxury isn’t about hiding your body or constantly chasing the next trend. It’s about proportions, self-worth, and clothes that give back to the wearer for a lifetime.

Where the film truly shifts from a standard fashion profile into a blueprint for corporate reform is inside the company’s factory walls in Solomeo, Italy.

At Cucinelli’s headquarters, workers are given keys to the facilities. There are no rigid clock-ins or draconian micromanagement, just a fundamental trust in the people who craft the product. Beyond that, roughly 20% of company profits are directly funneled back into “beautifying humanity,” from renovating the medieval village of Solomeo to maintaining public parks and community spaces.

The defining moment of this philosophy took place in March 2020. I’m sure we all remember where we were during that time. As global markets froze and uncertainty swept through the entire world, Cucinelli hosted a call with his entire workforce (around 9,000 people across the brand’s ecosystem). His message wasn’t about cutting costs or thinning out payroll. Instead, he made a firm, explicit commitment: For the next two years, he promised zero layoffs, guaranteed full salaries, and pledged that the company would not ask its suppliers for discounts. That’s enough to make anyone ask, “Where do I sign up?” In an era where tech giants and media houses routinely announce mass layoffs via automated emails, Cucinelli’s decision was a stark reminder that executive leadership is, at its core, a moral choice.

The documentary closes with two quiet, visually stunning scenes that are still etched in my mind. The first is an impossibly long family dinner table stretched across an open field in Italy. But the people sitting around it aren’t just Cucinelli’s immediate relatives. It’s his extended work family. A literal visual representation of what happens when a business shares its prosperity instead of hoarding it at the top.

The final image returns to a recurring motif throughout the film: Cucinelli playing cards. As a young man, he spent hours in local Italian bars cutting decks. Throughout the documentary, we see him at the table, but the final scene reveals who sits across from him. He isn’t playing against a rival designer or a corporate competitor. He’s playing against his younger self. It’s a striking metaphor for how Cucinelli operates. From a young boy guiding cows through Umbrian fields—obsessing over making sure the plow lines were perfectly straight—to building one of the most respected fashion houses in history, his focus has never been on beating the competition. It’s always been about self-mastery, controlling what you can control, and striving to be a better version of yourself than you were yesterday. That’s the ultimate main-character energy flex.

title: What Is “Skin Preservation,” & Why Is It Everywhere Right Now?
text:
What Is “Skin Preservation,” & Why Is It Everywhere Right Now?

So often in the beauty space, trends are little more than repackaged ideas from decades past. The term anti-aging, for example, has been rightly scrutinized for years, gradually giving way to a new buzzword that’s popping up not only in the healthcare space, but in beauty, as well: longevity. 

Where anti-aging positions wrinkles, dullness, and other visible signs of time as problems to fear and fix, skin longevity — and now, its close cousin, skin preservation, which I’ll get to shortly — is rooted in maintaining healthy skin for the long haul. Rather than chasing quick fixes or making you feel guilty about your choices, the goal is to support your skin with consistent habits and ingredients that help it look its best for as long as possible. (We’ve already seen this shift in products like Tatcha’s The Longevity Memory Cream, a firm R29 favorite, and Paula’s Choice CellularYouth Longevity Serum, both of which lean into the idea of protecting skin’s future rather than reversing its past.)

Most recently, there’s No7’s new Prime Forever collection: a four-piece skincare routine built around the concept of preserving skin before visible aging really begins to accelerate.  

DashDividers_1_500x100

What is “skin preservation,” & how does it differ from “anti-aging”? 

Skin longevity and skin preservation are essentially two sides of the same coin: helping your skin look and function at its best for as long as possible. What I was more interested in, however, was how that concept differs from the traditional idea of anti-aging as it’s been marketed for decades. 

Multiple factors contribute to accelerated skin aging. Free radicals create oxidative stress that damages skin cells, UVA and UVB rays break down collagen and cause pigmentation, and naturally occurring enzymes gradually degrade collagen and elastin, leading to loss of firmness over time. “Skin preservation is less about the quick fix, whereas even a few years ago it was more about, ‘I want immediate gratification. I want to see instant results,'” says New York-based dermatologist Dr. Marisa Garshick. “In general, people are taking a much more proactive approach with their health, and I think we’re definitely seeing that with skin, too.” In other words, instead of waiting until concerns appear, there’s a new focus toward building a routine that helps slow down visible changes before they happen — a subtle but fascinating shift in how we think about (and talk about) skin. 

All of that brings me to No7, where I recently got an early look at the Prime Forever range. Prime Forever is somewhat niche in that it’s uniquely suited to people around my age, when the earliest signs of aging are beginning to emerge. At 32, I have very few fine lines or wrinkles, and still benefit from the naturally bouncy, collagen-rich skin of my twenties. I credit that largely to good genetics, a daily sunscreen habit, and staying out of the sun whenever possible — but everyone’s skin ages eventually, and I’m more interested in keeping mine as resilient and radiant as possible. 

That proactive, ounce-of-prevention approach isn’t unique to me — far from it. “Most people don’t want to dramatically change what they look like,” Dr. Garshick tells me. “They just want to keep looking and feeling good.” And that’s exactly where skin preservation fits in: maintaining what you have rather than trying to undo years of accumulated damage later. 

Keep reading for my review of each No7 Prime Forever product and why they deserve a spot in your skincare regimen.  

DashDividers_1_500x100

Prime Forever Transformative Gel-Oil-Milk Cleanser, $19.99

The four-step routine begins with the Prime Forever Transformative Gel-Oil-Milk Cleanser, which dispenses as a gel before emulsifying into a silky, milky texture with water. Packed with glycerin to help draw moisture into the skin, plus antioxidant-rich vitamin E, it left my face feeling clean without that tight, stripped feeling. The texture is absolutely divine, and I find it works best as a luxurious morning cleanse or as the second step after an oil cleanser in the evening.

Prime Forever Preservation Serum, $39.99

Next comes the Prime Forever Preservation Serum, a lightweight formula that tackles multiple concerns at once. Alongside hydrating hyaluronic acid, it features niacinamide to help brighten and support the skin barrier, plus peptides that work to boost collagen and elastin over time. Despite packing in so many actives, it didn’t irritate my sensitive, breakout-prone skin one bit. (Also, the texture is incredibly silky and absorbed almost instantly; my skin practically drank it up.) It layers beautifully under moisturizer, never feeling sticky or pilling, making it an easy addition to both morning and nighttime routines.

Prime Forever Weightless Moisturizer, $39.99

An unexpected standout from the collection was the Prime Forever Weightless Moisturizer. Despite its cushiony gel texture, it delivers the kind of lasting hydration I’d normally expect from a much richer cream. Alongside hydrating humectants like glycerin and sodium hyaluronate, and the range’s signature peptide-and-antioxidant complex, it leaves skin looking plump and feeling comfortably moisturized without crossing into greasy territory. This is true for the entire Prime Forever lineup, but the textures really impressed me; if I were testing these blind, I’d assume they came from a luxury beauty counter rather than the drugstore aisle. 

Prime Forever SPF50 Primer, $34.99

Last but certainly not least is the Prime Forever SPF 50 Primer, which serves as the final step in your morning skincare routine. While it’s designed to prep skin for makeup, I’d happily wear it on its own thanks to its smoothing finish and broad-spectrum sun protection. Formulated with vitamin E and soothing aloe vera, it helps keep skin comfortable throughout the day while chemical UV filters provide completely transparent SPF 50 protection without even a whisper of white cast. What impressed me most, though, was the finish: it softens the look of texture, keeps excess shine at bay, and leaves my skin looking naturally radiant rather than starkly matte. SPF-infused primers are somewhat of a growing category, and I’m generally in favor of anything that makes UV protection feel more effortless. Still, think of this as a bonus rather than replacing your primary sunscreen to ensure you’re getting adequate UV protection.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Final Thoughts

\In a skincare landscape where expensive products and even more expensive in-office treatments like neuromodulators, fillers, and lasers claim to turn back the clock, I was honestly impressed at No7’s Prime Forever range. The formulas feel luxurious to use, but the prices remain relatively accessible, ranging from $20 to $39. And as gratifying as it is to see fast results, testing this routine is something that will inevitably require patience on my end; given where my skin is currently at, it’s likely that I won’t be able to truly appreciate the results of practicing safe sun and having a good skincare routine until five, maybe even 10, years from now. But you know what they say about marathons and sprints.

title: Saturn Retrograde In Aries Is Here — & You’ll Need To Set Some Boundaries
text:
Saturn Retrograde In Aries Is Here — & You’ll Need To Set Some Boundaries

Mark your calendars because as of July 26th, another planet will shift into its retrograde orbit: Saturn in Aries. From July 26th to December 10th, Saturn will make a cosmic U-turn, forcing us to face our fears. Michelle Tea, spiritualist and author of several books, says “Saturn retrograde can be a real ass-kicking for relationships, but necessary.” The author of upcoming book, Free Love: Adventures in Marriage and Polyamory, continues, “If things have been sliding, neglected, ignored, Saturn gives you another chance to do right. Saturn is not merciless — Saturn roots for us! — but Saturn warns us as well to not waste but we’ve been given, including a second chance!” 

Don’t be too disheartened though as Saturn retrograde isn’t necessarily a bad time for us to plan for the future. When the austere planet begins to moonwalk, it offers a moment of reflection in which we can plot our next moves, so get ready. It’s imperative we know how to temper the energy and pursue our goals without being too pushy. Saturn retrograde offers us the chance to create a game plan that fits our daily demands, lifestyle, and schedule. We aren’t try-hards; on the contrary, we’re able to attain our goals without stressing over the outcome. The path to success may not look like what we thought it would, but it takes us to where we need to be.

This retrograde is a moment in time when we will boss up in all our endeavors. Saturn’s backspin offers us the chance to take charge and to elevate our businesses to the next level. When direct, Saturn represents company management or the principal imposing rules in school; the opposite is true when retrograde. Saturn’s regressive state evolves into something more, giving us the wherewithal to implement new visions and heightening our desire to innovate, allowing us to impose radical values on societal norms and standards. We aren’t afraid to take a stand.

Setting healthy aspirations can be challenging because we are assessing our circumstances intuitively. Rigidity is not on the agenda, which is why adhering to a schedule is useless. Life as we know it is in flux, so go with the flow. Use the retrograde to revise programs, routines, or habits. But do not try to change everything all at once, because it won’t go over so well and will be difficult to stick to once the retrograde completes its cycle. We need to do research and refine our situation before getting on board with a new program to ensure it aligns with our long-term goals.

Despite all the retrograde madness occurring at the moment from Mercury, Neptune, and Pluto (in September, Uranus starts diving backward), Saturn’s backsplash urges us to level up our relationships. As a result, we may be more inclined to connect with others intimately. Pursuing a relationship could be concerning if we do not choose to yield our passions. The caveat is that jumping in too soon before getting to know the other person can create problems if we aren’t careful, so make the effort to get to know them and take it slow. Intentional dating is advisable to ensure our needs and wants are satisfied.

The key ingredients for a successful Saturn retrograde are implementing boundaries — not only for others but for ourselves as well. We should stay in our lane and not swerve into criticizing others or casting judgment until we know the full story. We expect the same from others, so we must practice what we preach.

title: Go Off, Sis: Jenee Naylor of HighLowLuxxe on Making a Plan and Letting Go of Perfection
text:
Go Off, Sis: Jenee Naylor of HighLowLuxxe on Making a Plan and Letting Go of Perfection

For Jenee Naylor, success requires a roadmap. Now, that doesn’t mean following a traditional path or climbing the corporate ladder, but rather looking to others for what is possible. ‘Seeing is believing,’ the founder of 12PM Studios tells host Erica Chidi Cohen, and now she hopes to inspire other Black women by sharing all that she’s learned. 

Before Jenee made her first major splash with her blog HighLowLuxxe, she got her start on the floor of a Target store in the DMV. She started managing a team of people and moving up the ranks. “I learned how to be a business person through that role,” she shares. She thrived in leadership, particularly because it allowed her to pour into others; she loved teaching, training, and getting people promoted; she was a campus recruiter for Howard. In many ways, it laid the foundation for what was to come. Working for a big store taught her the value of strategy and everything having a place.  “So much of my personality is about being efficient and making the most of things.” 

Her blog, HighLowLuxxe, was “something clever that represented me,” Jenee says it was true to who she was at the time, mostly shopping fast fashion but splurging on something with her bonus check. It was the perfect blend of Jenee’s expertise and her sharing what she was learning about the world of luxury. Part of what made the blog such a success was Jenee’s honest approach to creating content. Sure, she’d have a flawless beat, but she’d shoot her videos in one take. And authenticity might be the key to her long-term success. “Consistency and longevity are hard to maintain if you are putting on an act,” she shares. 

It takes a lot of bravery to walk away from something when it’s working, and working well. Although HighLowLuxxe was a resounding success, Jenee felt called to build something in her own name. She

walked away from high/low luxe to build 12PM Studios, her extremely chic sunglasses company. Why eyewear? For one, it’s “the only thing I care enough about to talk about every day,” Jenee laughs. But also, once Jenee reached the point of success where others were photographing her, she realized sunglasses can offer a bit of protection, a very chic shield from the outside world. So, she looked at what was out there, how others were succeeding, trusted her instincts, and built herself another roadmap. Learn more about how she got from managing a Target to selling her products in Target in this episode of Go Off, Sis.

title: It’s The Summer Of Chunky Jewelry Maxxing
text:
It’s The Summer Of Chunky Jewelry Maxxing

This summer’s biggest trend, quite literally, is chunky jewelry. Unlike most seasonal trends, this one is not going anywhere anytime soon. Once you fall for chunky jewelry, it quietly becomes part of your personal style, to the point where people can’t imagine you without it.

No one embraced the spirit of chunky jewelry quite like the late, great fashion icon Iris Apfel. Long before oversized bangles and sculptural necklaces took over the fashion world, she built an unforgettable personal style around maximalist jewelry. Her bold accessories became a reflection of her fearless personality, making it almost impossible to picture her without them. And from what we’re seeing now, maybe we’re all channeling our inner Iris Apfel this summer.

Whether it’s a beach day, a city stroll, dinner plans, or a night out, chunky jewelry belongs everywhere. After all, an accessory is the finishing touch that can completely transform any outfit.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bella 🦋 (@bellahadid)

Although the chunky jewelry trend can be traced back to the 2010s, fashion has been moving in this direction again over the past few years. Schiaparelli was among the first to bring statement jewelry back into the spotlight in 2023 with its surrealist accessories. And as maximalism gradually made its way from the runway into everyday wardrobes, surrealist jewelry evolved into something far more wearable.

This change became even more visible on the latest runways, with Sarah Burton’s debut Givenchy SS26 collection showcasing oversized necklaces and statement earrings, while Zimmermann’s SS26 collection featured sculptural jewelry alongside its romantic summer aesthetic.

This summer, the bigger the better. Less layering of dainty pieces, and more styling with larger accessories. Sometimes, all it takes is one great find to become the centerpiece of your wardrobe. My go-to summer outfit formula starts with a white tank top, relaxed linen trousers, oversized sunglasses, kitten heel mules, and as much chunky jewelry as I can get. Colorful resin bangles, sculptural earrings, and playful shapes always work together. The only rule I stick to is keeping each jewelry category consistent: silver with silver, resin with resin. Another key element is to let just one jewelry category do the talking.

During the day, style a sheer cape top with denim shorts, flip-flops, and oversized resin bangles for an effortless summer look. For evenings, pair a simple midi summer dress with sculptural gold earrings, chunky gold rings, and strappy heels. For me, everything else in your outfit can change, but a great chunky ring stack can remain your signature finishing touch. The trick is this: chunky rings are the ultimate day-to-night jewelry, and, sometimes, even piece you’ll wear for a lifetime, like Dua Lipa’s chunky engagement ring, which has quickly become one of the most talked-about jewelry pieces of the year.

In the summer, chunky jewelry can take the form of an abstract shape, like fruit, flowers, or seashells. Pair oversized shell earrings with a monochrome matching set for an effortless vacation look, or let a stack of colorful resin bangles elevate a simple white sundress. One of my personal favorites in my jewelry drawer is a pair of oversized cherry earrings, which I happily wear with everything from a white tank and denim shorts to a simple midi dress. Whichever way you choose to style it, chunky jewelry is the perfect trend to express yourself and be as loud as you want, like Apfel proudly did.

title: Nicolandria Is (Reportedly) Over. Why Do We Care So Much About Celebrity Breakups?
text:
Nicolandria Is (Reportedly) Over. Why Do We Care So Much About Celebrity Breakups?

Love is dead. Or so it feels for many fans after celebrity couples announce their breakups. Love Island Season 7 stars Olandria Carthen and Nic Vansteenberghe have broken up after a year of dating, PEOPLE exclusively reports. The popular couple “decided to part ways” as, the PEOPLE source claims, “the distance between them and their busy schedules made it challenging to maintain their connection.” The source continues: “They still remain close friends. They share a deep love and respect for each other and will always support one another whenever possible.”

2026 has also ushered in other high profile celebrity breakups, like Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff (a Qualley source told PEOPLE that the couple is “figuring things out” amid the split), Ariana Grande and Ethan Slater (she has since reconnected with her ex, Ricky Alvarez), Sue Bird and Megan Rapinoe (lesbians around the world were devastated) and Megan Thee Stallion and Klay Thompson, just to name a few. Each of these breakups made headlines (for various reasons) and caused our timelines to speculate, rage, mourn, or all three. It’s natural to be upset when a couple you think you know — or one you were simply rooting hard for — breaks up. When it comes to Nic and Olandria, they have a very specific microscope on their relationship, and the amount of parasocial obsession with their love story seemed to reach heights the internet had never seen. There are the “contract is up!” people who think they were never really dating in the first place, the “love is dead!” camp who pinned all their romantic hopes on the duo, and the “I don’t believe it” folks who are living in denial that PEOPLE magazine is a celeb-friendly source often used by publicists as an unofficial “official” way to get news to the public. It’s safe to say that Nicolandria is done. What’s clear for sure is that everyone has an opinion, and people really care about celebrity breakups.

In 2023, after the breakup of Joe Manganiello and Sofia Vergara, Alicia Vrajlal wrote for Refinery29 that, “Admittedly, I’m one of [the people who mourn celeb breakups]. Like many fans, I was devastated when I heard the news and overwhelmed with a sense of sorrow and disbelief. It can’t be true. Everything seemed to be going so well. I almost wanted to cry. “

But in a world where Hollywood splits are so common, and celebrity worship is becoming at once more intense than ever and more scrutinized, why do we care so much about the relationship breakdowns of famous people we’ve never met?

‘Relationship goals’ is a term often thrown around when it comes to celebrities, because they tend to publicly portray the ideal or fantasy of what a relationship looks like or can aspire to be. But our understanding of #RelationshipGoals has shifted. In 2021, we wrote that, “Not only do #RelationshipGoals fetishize an image that’s curated and not real, they also glorify a type of love that prioritizes staying together (aka building a brand) over anything else.” When we look at stars and project them to be attractive yet down-to-earth, and have busy careers but still find time for dates and cute grocery trips together, we are inadvertently creating the idea that their romance can survive the odds, no matter what. In reality, everything ends, and we don’t know these people. That said, it’s natural to be curious and to care.

“Many of us are interested in celebrities and other public figures and are naturally curious about their lives,” psychologist Dr Marny Lishman tells Refinery29. “At some level, their lives are so unattainable and almost fantasy-like to us, but at another level, many of the same trials and tribulations they endure are not unlike our own.”

It’s because of this that we live vicariously through them when we’re single, and unconsciously strive for the relationship success they have when we’re in a relationship of our own. With that being said, it only makes sense that when a celebrity couple calls it quits, we too feel a sudden loss. We are worried about the Nicolandria hive.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Ericka Hart, M.Ed. (@ihartericka)

In 2023, Nina, 23, said she felt this loss when Lisa Bonet and Jason Momoa broke up in January 2022. At the time, when Phoebe Bridgers and Paul Mescal (who is now dating Gracie Abrams) called time on their romance, Nina was also shook.

“While I definitely don’t get upset about all the famous breakups, these ones truly made me sad,” she tells Refinery29, explaining she was inspired by certain aspects of each couple’s relationships.

“When couples you look up to split up, it kind of gives you a ‘romance and love are dead’ feeling, which sucks. They gave the impression that even relationships with barriers — age differences, dealing with so much fame and gossip or personal drama — stood a chance.”

Lishman explains that we’re often only exposed to one version of reality when it comes to celebrity relationships. This makes our disbelief that much stronger when the romances collapse.

“We idolize their relationships too as we idolize the celebrity, so when the ‘seemingly perfect’ relationship ends, we grieve for the ending of what we perceived as perfection,” says Lishman.

“We see a fairly edited version of reality, so it’s hard to understand why a seemingly perfect relationship would end. At times we are shocked because it ‘looked’ so good.”

Nina agrees, saying that she has “put celebrity couples on a pedestal” in the past, looking to them for “inspiration and confirmation of romance in the world.” So when it all comes crumbling down, it’s a bit of a reality check.

“When they break up, it’s just a sad reminder that no one is immune to the realities and difficulties of love and commitment,” she says.

Lishman explains that this realization is very normal. While it’s hard for many of us to process the news when a seemingly perfect celeb couple breaks up, we know that to some degree (without the fame and fortune), they are just like us.

“They are complex, imperfect creatures that go through highs and lows in life, just like we do. They lose love, they break up, they grieve, they get rejected — just like the rest of us.”

Social media has only exacerbated our passionate responses to celebrity splits. In a time when we watch so many celebrities carefully curate their TikToks with ‘relatable’ couple vids, or flirt up a storm in the comments section, how can we not get deeply invested in their blossoming romances?

“Social media allows us to connect more with them [celebrities], and also be more informed about what’s going in their lives. It gives us more information than traditional media, so we seem to be more invested,” says Lishman.

We’re also seeing more celebrities who find love on a reality TV dating shows (like Nic and Olandria) or on the set of a film, which makes us feel like we’ve been on the journey with them — from the first date to the breakup announcement post on Instagram. And in some cases (like Love Island couples), we actually have. No matter how hard you felt it when High School Musical stars Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens split in 2010, we weren’t privy to watching their entire love story play out on camera. Sure, we watched the young love blossom from HSM 1 to 3, and it’s hard not to recall their affection and red carpet cuteness fondly, it’s a whole different beast when a couple’s first kiss and every flirtation is caught on camera. That’s why we’re in the depths of people being extremely not normal about celebrity breakups (just look at how some Swifties still talk about Joe Alwyn). For the celebs, navigating the public scrutiny also seems to be tougher than ever.

Olandria just had to clap back at unverified gossip platform, DeuxMoi, for circulating a rumor that she’s been hooking up with Travis Scott. Olandria denied this claim and commented, “I hope you have your lawyers ready bc I have mine.” According to Cosmo, Olandria’s comment has been deleted or hidden from the public. DeuxMoi confirmed in a pinned comment, “Update: Olandria denied(?) this rumor but blocked this account so her comment, which was pinned was not showing it was from her.”

As the likes of Nic, Olandria, and other celebs, continue to navigate their respective breakups, there will always be fans who are still rooting for them, who will shamelessly keep caring about their favorite celebrity couples (and their breakups), in the hope that there will be just as many moments filled with joy as there will be grief. Some of these people need to go outside and touch grass, while others (like us!) are invested in healthy, completely normal ways. (It’s a good thing Tom Holland and Zendaya are going to stay together forever, right? Right!?) These are people’s real lives, but often it can feel like we’re still watching a fictional love story play out, or that the stakes are just who’s coupled up in a villa. That’s why you see so many people unable to let go of their fave celeb couples — for better and for worse.

After all, how many of us have secretly harbored the hope that Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck will rekindle their flame one day (again!)? For some couples, a breakup is certainly the right decision. But as fans, it’s easy to hope that some of our favorite couples will get back together (again, think Bennifer 2.0, or Justin and Hailey Bieber or OTP Tom and Zendaya). Regardless of whether the split is temporary or permanent, we just need to remember that hope is not dead, and neither is love.

This article referencing celebrity breakups was originally published, in part, in 2023. It has since been updated to include recent celeb relationship news.

title: Bikini Tops Are the New Going-Out Top: Here’s How To Style Them
text:
Bikini Tops Are the New Going-Out Top: Here’s How To Style Them

A heatwave? No problem. As temperatures continue to rise, bikini tops are no longer just beachwear; they’ve become a practical and stylish solution for summer style, whether you’re on vacation or in the city. This is the trend we’ve all been waiting for, because your bikini top definitely deserves a chance beyond the pool side this summer.

There’s just something about an outfit that feels slightly unfinished that perfectly captures the carefree spirit of summer and gives me a real sense of freedom. Even when I’m not on holiday, summer itself inspires me to be more creative with the way I dress.

This season, the bikini top has evolved from being that “just in case” item tossed into your vacation suitcase to becoming one of the go-to tops for grabbing a coffee, stopping by the market on the weekend, or heading out for dinner. Thanks especially to Dua Lipa’s summer wardrobe, the line between swimwear and citywear feels more blurred than ever this season.

There are countless ways to style your bikini top, but with the rising temperatures and ever-changing trends, it can be more confusing than ever to know where to start. Need some styling tips? There are a few celebrity-approved ways to wear the trend. From Kylie Jenner’s latest bikini rotation and Gigi Hadid‘s effortless off-duty style to the festival style inspired by Charli XCX’s Brat era, your starting point for making this trend your own is ahead. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Hailey Rhode Bieber (@haileybieber)

Swimwear design is also starting to shift in parallel with this trend. Rather than relying on traditional swimwear prints and beach-inspired aesthetics, recent collections are increasingly drawing inspiration from everyday city life.

For example, in the recent KHY x Frankies Bikinis collaboration, founder Francesca Aiello told WWD that the collection was inspired by her shared love of Los Angeles with Kylie Jenner, hoping that it “felt as unique and sexy as the city itself.” So, rather than looking to the beach as its primary source of inspiration, the collection looks to the city’s aesthetic for a modern approach.

How To Style Bikini Tops

And just like that, this summer’s unofficial “holy trinity” has practically formed itself: a timeless bikini top, comfortable flip-flops you can walk all day in, and a hand fan you’re never willing to put down. Suddenly, getting dressed during a heatwave feels much less complicated. My favorite styling trick is letting colorful bikini details and string straps peek out from under a tiny white tank top and barrel-leg trousers. 

Throw a lightweight linen shirt over your shoulders or tie it around your waist, then accessorize with chunky gold earrings, layered necklaces, and a tote bag. Just a few touches make the outfit feel intentional rather than accidental, turning the bikini top into a natural part of your everyday summer wardrobe.

If you’re spending your sunny days in the city rather than on vacation, take inspiration from Dua Lipa’s effortless vacation aesthetic by pairing a black triangle bikini top with relaxed denim shorts, a lightweight oversized jacket, and simple strappy sandals. Boldly colored bikinis with relaxed jeans also simply give an instant cool-girl feel.

For a summer night out, you can swap the shorts for fun pants, adding a metallic bikini top, black sunglasses, and kitten mules. The look is instantly evening-ready, making it a great choice for a club or festival.

My personal favorite is wearing a polka-dot bikini top over a white baby tee with a midi skirt, flip-flops, and a mini handbag. The fun part of this trend is that there are no rules; it’s just an experiment with different silhouettes, colors, prints, and accessories until you find your own style.
